section_summary: This section concerns postwar currency and foreign trade in Japan and Korea, including remittances, blocked yen, trade financing, and competing proposals for a yen-dollar exchange rate. It contains diplomatic correspondence, SCAP reports, Japanese policy recommendations, private inquiries, and a newspaper article on inflation and sterling trade. The final pages trace State Department debate over whether and when to establish a Japanese commercial exchange rate.

subfiles.title: Department reply on Korean radiotelegraph service
subfiles.from: Cecil G. Harrison, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department discusses Korean radiotelegraph service and requests the company's response.
subfiles.summary: Closing page of a Department letter requesting comment.

subfiles.title: RCA radiotelegraph service and won holdings in Korea
subfiles.about: RCA plans wider service in occupied Korea but limits payment to dollars because it cannot convert its growing won holdings.
subfiles.summary: The company proposes using Korean postal facilities to collect and deliver radiograms from September 1, 1947. Its Seoul receipts greatly exceed local expenses, leaving substantial unusable won balances. Attached tables give accumulated holdings, disbursements, expenses, and Korea traffic income.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese export markets and rayon prices
subfiles.about: Dunford asks how specified export markets fit Far Eastern Commission categories and whether a world rayon price has been studied.
subfiles.summary: Requests classification of listed markets and information on rayon pricing.

subfiles.title: Notes for reply on rayon and export categories
subfiles.about: An internal note considers Dunford's questions and possible wording about rayon prices.
subfiles.summary: Notes uncertainty about a world rayon price and cites Japanese rayon price estimates.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dunford on export currencies and rayon
subfiles.about: Whitman explains Japanese exports' dollar or barter settlement and says the Commission has not studied world rayon prices.
subfiles.summary: Explains currency constraints on listed markets and SCAP's responsibility for implementing export pricing policy.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about sending money to Japan
subfiles.about: Shimpo asks whether relaxed remittance rules allow individuals to send money to relatives in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests return-wire details on family remittances.

subfiles.title: Reply on remittances to Japan
subfiles.about: The Department explains the monthly limit, yen conversion, payment certificates, and available transfer bank.
subfiles.summary: States a $1,000 monthly recipient limit and identifies National City Bank as able to make transfers.

subfiles.title: Bagulesco's request for restitution and other assistance
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports General Bagulesco's renewed effort to recover Swiss francs converted into yen during the war.
subfiles.summary: An enclosed November 17 conversation records Bagulesco's requests for hard currency restitution, shipment of art from Peking, and possible United States travel. He describes wartime mistreatment and financial hardship; the Embassy seeks information on his account.

subfiles.title: Investigation of General Bagulesco's bank account
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sebald reports the remaining yen credit and rejects Bagulesco's claim to special protection pending evidence.
subfiles.summary: Yokohama Specie Bank records show a ¥47,700 balance on a wartime letter of credit bought with Swiss francs, but current controls prevent conversion outside Japan. A November 22 Army intelligence summary disputes Bagulesco's assertions of pro-Allied sympathies and Japanese internment, describing public support for the Axis instead. The mission finds insufficient grounds for a guarantee under SCAPIN 1364.

subfiles.title: Department transmission of Bagulesco investigation
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Sebald's report and intelligence summary for the Embassy's information.
subfiles.summary: Transmits adverse findings on Bagulesco's claim for protected funds.

subfiles.title: Department charge slip
subfiles.about: A records form logs files charged to staff.
subfiles.summary: Lists charged records, including exchange file 894.5151.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of request for documents
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department cancels an earlier document request and asks for any charges incurred.
subfiles.summary: Cancels instruction A-110 of December 5.

subfiles.title: Yen-dollar ratios in Japanese trade
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sebald transmits tables on yen-dollar relationships in Japanese trade and price trends.
subfiles.summary: Reports wide variation in yen-dollar ratios across commodities and notes export dollar prices do not track yen costs. The despatch describes government trade, private contracts, and Japanese and United States price comparisons; its referenced tables are not present on these pages.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about a Sumitomo Bank yen draft
subfiles.about: Arai asks how to protect or collect a prewar Sumitomo Bank draft payable in yen at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Arai encloses his same-day inquiry to the Office of Alien Property concerning a draft bought in Seattle for Yo Yamashita. He asks whether a claim against vested assets must be filed or payment sought in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Sumitomo Bank draft
subfiles.from: Stanley D. Metzger, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses whether it can assist collection of a yen draft in Japan.
subfiles.summary: It defers the vested-assets claim question to the Office of Alien Property and suggests direct correspondence with the Japanese bank.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting Far Eastern Commission presentation
subfiles.about: Wisner asks that the Commission hear a United States statement on financing Japanese foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: Requests early presentation before bank loan agreements are finalized.

subfiles.title: Statement to the Far Eastern Commission on trade financing
subfiles.about: The statement announces SCAP steps to implement the Commission's interim import-export policy.
subfiles.summary: Notifies Commission members of planned financing measures and an implementing circular.

subfiles.title: Explanatory memorandum on the export-import revolving fund
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains proposed use and safeguards for Japanese gold, silver, and precious assets in trade finance.
subfiles.summary: Describes a separate fund for import financing, possible asset sales for needed currencies, equal purchase opportunities for Commission members, and recycling export proceeds.

subfiles.title: Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund rules
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The circular establishes and regulates a revolving fund for Japanese imports and exports.
subfiles.summary: It places the fund under a SCAP-designated controller and begins it with roughly $137 million in gold or equivalent assets. It specifies eligible receipts and expenditures, borrowing authority, reserves, asset-sale safeguards, monthly reporting, and liquidation on a transfer of authority or peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Replacement record-copy notice
subfiles.about: The notice identifies a copy of Tokyo despatch 1473 as the replacement record copy.
subfiles.summary: Records that the original action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Japanese government views on exchange problems
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards Japanese recommendations for a general exchange rate and interim commodity-specific export rates.
subfiles.summary: The despatch analyzes the Japanese preference for multiple export exchange factors, the risk of inflation or losses under a single rate, and administrative difficulties. The first enclosure recommends a general rate, a balancing formula, a Yen Committee, and exchange controls. The second lists Exchange Committee members across Japanese ministries, boards, and banks.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Tokyo despatch 1473
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A second filed copy repeats the despatch on Japanese exchange-rate recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the covering analysis of the Japanese proposal; its enclosures appear in the preceding copy.

subfiles.title: Netherlands views on a Japanese exchange rate
subfiles.about: Netherlands representatives favor one Japanese exchange rate and consultation before its establishment.
subfiles.summary: They oppose a persistent multiple-rate or free-exchange system, discuss subsidies and limited exporter retention of currency, and prefer setting the rate in Washington after consulting interested governments and the International Monetary Fund.

subfiles.title: British Treasury concerns about private trade and yen exchange
subfiles.about: Percival conveys British Treasury concerns about proposed private trade arrangements with Japan.
subfiles.summary: He urges a flexible, usable yen rate for licensed trade, asks how invisible payments and military-rate conversions would work, and offers further discussion.

subfiles.title: Tokyo confirms no expense on canceled request
subfiles.about: Sebald answers the Department's cancellation telegram.
subfiles.summary: Reports that no expense was incurred.

subfiles.title: Revised tables on yen-dollar relationships
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The mission transmits revised tables for exchange-rate discussions.
subfiles.summary: Describes nine tables covering trade ratios, projected 1948 trade, and Japanese and United States price indexes.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Allied Council exchange-rate committee
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department asks SCAP's views on General Shang's proposed Allied Council experts committee.
subfiles.summary: Requests information on the suggestion and anticipated reply.

subfiles.title: SCAP rejects Allied Council experts committee
subfiles.about: SCAP explains its opposition to an Allied Council committee on the yen exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: The proposal was dropped after SCAP objected that another advisory committee would duplicate work and intrude on administration.

subfiles.title: Remittances from Japan in the Sotera Fernandez case
subfiles.about: Officials discuss how someone in Japan may remit money abroad.
subfiles.summary: Remittances require dollars or acceptable instruments; yen cannot be remitted. The memorandum suggests bank or family assistance.

subfiles.title: London despatch and article on Japanese inflation and sterling trade
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy London
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Malcolm Muggeridge's article advocating renewed sterling trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The February 2 article describes inflation, weak production, occupation costs, and difficulties selling Japanese textiles for dollars. Muggeridge argues that access to sterling-area raw materials and markets is vital to recovery. He discusses barter, proposed bank credits backed by Japanese gold, reparations uncertainty, and the need for faster British-American negotiations.

subfiles.title: Army referral of Dean Sherry's yen conversion request
subfiles.from: Office of the Judge Advocate General, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: The Army refers former prisoner Dean Sherry's request to convert yen paid by Japanese captors.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Sherry's letter and an Army circular for State Department consideration.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Sherry's request
subfiles.about: The legal office forwards the inquiry and asks for information on Japanese payments to American prisoners.
subfiles.summary: Requests a paragraph seeking Sherry's total pay and its calculation method.

subfiles.title: Dean Sherry's request to exchange prisoner-of-war pay
subfiles.to: Office of the Chief of Finance
subfiles.about: Sherry asks how to exchange about 3,900 yen received from Japanese captors.
subfiles.summary: Seeks a dollar conversion method and expected amount.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Dean Sherry
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department cannot give Sherry a definite dollar settlement for his yen and seeks details for war-claims research.
subfiles.summary: Explains the yen's diminished value and uncertainty about settlement, then asks for the total pay received and how it was calculated.

subfiles.title: NA objection to proposed exchange-rate cable
subfiles.about: NA withholds approval of a proposed cable on Japan's commercial exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: It urges waiting for Kennan's return and asks for justification of a proposed mission.

subfiles.title: Whitman resubmits proposed exchange-rate cable
subfiles.about: Whitman argues for a mission to speed decisions on Japan's commercial exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: He cites SCAP interest, the returned Kennan mission, foreign governments' concerns, disagreement over multiple rates, and the need for current data and officials empowered to negotiate in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to clear exchange-rate mission proposal
subfiles.about: Green supports a Tokyo mission to establish a Japanese exchange rate promptly.
subfiles.summary: Recommends a mission favoring early action, with broad authority, in Japan by June 1948.

subfiles.title: Questions about exchange-rate policy paper
subfiles.about: Allison questions responsibility for fixing the rate, the proposed mission, and consultation procedures.
subfiles.summary: Raises Japanese-government responsibility, the role of the Inter-Allied Trade Board and Far Eastern Commission, and consultation with the returning Draper group.

subfiles.title: Note to Butterworth on Japanese responsibility
subfiles.about: The note relays Hamilton's reservations about SCAP setting Japan's exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: Calls attention to Japanese responsibility and the reason for bypassing Far Eastern Commission review.

subfiles.title: Hamilton withdraws clearance pending Draper report
subfiles.about: Hamilton recommends delaying exchange-rate action until the Draper group's report is complete.
subfiles.summary: He removes his initials from the proposed cable and policy paper because the group considers conditions too unstable.

subfiles.title: Reply to Allison on exchange-rate mission and jurisdiction
subfiles.about: The memorandum defends SCAP control and a special mission for an early Japanese exchange-rate decision.
subfiles.summary: Argues that transferring the technical decision to Japan would delay it, describes competing June and year-end positions within SCAP, and identifies the Inter-Allied Trade Board. The memorandum continues beyond this section.
